newsitem.title: JAPAN: Disney arranges refinancing deal -- report.
newsitem.headline: Disney arranges refinancing deal -- report.

text.p: Walt Disney Co has negotiated a deal to refinance a 73.4 billion yen loan which is backed by future royalties from its theme park in Japan, the Financial Times reported on Monday.
The arrangement, called a Dated Widely Auctioned Royalty Financing Structure (Dwarfs), is designed to reduce the interest cost on the loan Disney originally took out in 1988.
It is also intended to eliminate risks associated with fluctuations in the dollar/yen rate during the remaining 11 years of the loan, the daily said.

With royalties earned from Tokyo Disneyland, Disney will service the loan at an annual rate of three percent, which is about half the rate it was paying on the securitised 20-year loan arranged by Citibank in 1988, the FT said.
Walt Disney's loan is backed by royalties in gate receipts and concession fess which it receives from Oriental Land, the operator of Tokyo Disneyland.

The report said that officials in the syndicate, comprised of lead-manager HSBC Markets, Citibank, the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan (LTCB) and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank (DKB), said that the refinancing has several unusual features. Unlike most securitised loans, payments will be made at a floating rate of interest rather than at a fixed rate.

The FT said HSBC Markets will conduct an auction at three-year intervals when the coupon paid to lenders rises from 30 basis points over the Japanese London Interbank Offered Rate to 60 basis points and 90 basis points, respectively.
Officials at LTCB and Dai-Ichi Kangyo said that they could not immediately comment on the report.
